rationale: The author asks how to keep arguments meant for a launched program from being parsed as this program's own commands and flags, a general question about existing argument handling with the launcher only as illustration.
The author asks why commands whose parents are not runnable do not appear under Available Commands and whether that is intentional, a why-question about existing help listing behavior.
The body asks either whether negative-number arguments work today or whether a Command could gain an AllowNegativeArgs field, so one requested outcome is a new API field.
The body reports that MarkPersistentFlagRequired did not produce the error the author expected when the flag was omitted, an actual-versus-expected report about his own command wiring.
The body states that the licensetext config field is ignored and that proper documentation would be helpful, claiming a defect and requesting a documentation change.
The author asks how the program is made to exit after --help is shown, a general question about the built-in help path and what the caller does with it.
The author asks whether the flag list can be printed without being sorted, with his two flags shown only as illustration.
The author asks whether there is a built-in way to declare and document a required positional argument rather than checking the args slice by hand.
The issue is a failure report that go install of the generator does not work, evidenced only by a screenshot and the statement that there are bugs to fix.
The author asks how one flag can be given a default value that depends on the value of another flag.
The author asks how to determine which flags were actually supplied on the command line rather than left at their defaults.
The author asks whether arguments or flags may be placed between a parent command and its subcommand.
The author asks whether the help command can be invoked programmatically on demand from inside a command.
The author asks whether a minimum number of positional arguments can be enforced without hand-written checks.
The author asks how to wire a debug flag into his own logging setup and shows that his init function runs before the flag is set, so answering means reasoning about his application code.
The author asks how several sibling subcommands can share one child command without declaring a separate copy for each.
The author asks whether autocompletion can be produced for the Windows cmd shell or only for linux and unix.
The author asks how persistent flag values can be reached inside an init function, noting they are still unset before Execute, with a minimal illustrative example.
The author asks whether there is a way to parse a plain string as if it had been given on the command line.
The author asks whether a watch-style CLI can be built where flags come first and the remaining tokens are passed through without typing a double dash.
The author asks how a value set in a pre-run hook is carried into Run and whether context.Context is supported for that.
The title and body ask for the deprecation message to be shown in help output, which is a request to change what is printed.
The body explains that the default help subcommand cannot be removed and asks for some mechanism to disable it, so the requested outcome is new behavior.
The author asks whether there is a way to tell that a command's Args field was set to NoArgs.
The author pastes his own program and asks whether there is an error in it because the boolean flags print true where he expected false.
The author asks whether there is a good way to reconstruct the original command-line invocation from inside Run or PreRun, showing his current approach only as illustration.
The author asks how code can be run at the root level for every subcommand after the flags have been parsed.
The author asks how flags are supplied when a command is exercised in a test, showing SetArgs and the resulting unknown flag message as illustration.
The author asks whether a default set of positional arguments for a subcommand can come from a config file.
The title alone asks whether output can be colorized and the body is empty, leaving it undetermined whether an existing capability or a new one is being asked about.
The issue asks that the nuclio project be added to the list of projects using this library, a documentation change rather than an information request.
The author asks how values captured by one command can be made available to other commands of the same CLI.
The author asks for the correct single call that makes a version subcommand produce the same output as the root command's --version.
The author asks how the root command can behave as one of its children, including that child's flags, without showing them in root help.
The author asks how completion output can be generated in the format of a shell other than the ones already produced.
The author asks whether the Global Flags section can be suppressed from a command's help output.
The author asks where argument validation belongs among Run, init and Execute, a question about the command lifecycle.
The author asks how the program exits once the built-in help has been displayed.
The author asks for the correct invocation syntax of the times example whose code he quotes from the project's own example.
The author asks how information produced in PersistentPreRun is passed to Run.
The body asks whether the init generator could simply take the package name from go.mod, so the requested outcome is a change to its behavior.
The author asks how to fit the library into his own repository layout of two microservices, and the answer depends entirely on that layout.
The author asks whether it can be determined that none of a command's flags were set without naming each flag.
The author asks why --version is reported as an unknown flag after he set the version template and what he missed.
The issue asks about an etcd entry in go.sum and suggests go mod tidy may be needed, so the requested outcome is dependency maintenance.
The author asks whether a flag value can be taken as an unparsed raw string so that its contents are not read as further flags.
The author asks whether the generator supports disabling copyright generation altogether.
The author asks whether a command can invoke a designated subcommand by default when none is named.
The author asks how a boolean flag left at its default is distinguished from one that was set.
The author asks whether the exit status produced for an unknown command can be changed from zero to one.
The author asks how to page a long list the way a git pager does, which concerns his program's output presentation rather than a capability of this library.
The author asks whether the trailing message telling the user to run help for usage can be disabled.
The author asks whether there is a cleaner way to mark the built-in version flag as deprecated than putting the notice in the version template.
The author asks how the flags of the command that is currently executing are obtained.
The author asks how to implement streaming output like the follow flag of kubectl logs, which concerns his own program's output loop rather than an existing library behavior.
The author asks how errors should be returned or printed from commands, with an appended wish that the README cover it.
The author asks how the name shown for the root command can differ from the application's own name.
The issue is a title stating that the output of git diff cannot be used as arguments plus a screenshot, so what is being asked cannot be determined without the image.
The author asks how one command can invoke other subcommands, describing the drawbacks he sees in calling Run or Execute directly.
The issue asks that an error be returned when the same flag is supplied more than once instead of the last value winning, a request for new behavior.
The author asks how behavior for unknown commands can be defined or how commands can be added at runtime, two alternatives serving one plugin-dispatch intent.
The author asks how the root command's Version can be set dynamically at build time.
The author asks how a completion that suggests a fixed list of words is written in Go using this library.
The author asks how the program can tell which of its commands was selected.
The issue asks where the documentation site's sources live, states they are not in this repository, and proposes that the approach be discussed.
The author asks whether variables can be shared across all the commands of one program.
The author reports that the PowerShell completion script generated by his older version does not work in his shell, so answering depends on his shell and version state.
The author asks how flag values can be validated as they are parsed and whether validation callbacks can be attached to flags.
The author asks how to satisfy a Go linter that forbids init functions, so the subject is his own code organization rather than library behavior.
The author asks how to avoid the global variables his linter complains about, a Go style question rather than a question about this library.
The author asks whether the entire deprecation message for a command can be customized, describing what the default message prints.
The author asks how mutually exclusive flags are defined, saying he found no documentation covering it.
The author quotes the three help customization methods and asks what each does and how the help template is written.
The issue asks that the generator command be changed to accept a file name and variable name and to run from the current directory.
The author asks why redirecting his command's output to a file yields an empty file, which depends on his test helper and the output writers he set.
The author asks how the global flags declared on the root command are read from within a subcommand.
The author asks how a command's status is passed to the post-run hook.
The author asks whether the licence handling he found in the repository can be used to manage custom software licence keys and asks for a working example.
The author asks whether a subcommand's result can be made available to its parent command.
The author asks whether flags whose values are file globs are supported.
The issue reports that with NoArgs set a boolean flag's value is rejected as an unknown command, an actual-versus-expected defect report.
The author asks how the automatically generated usage line naming a command placeholder can be removed.
The author asks how the automatically added help subcommand can be removed from the root command's listing.
The author asks why required-flag validation runs after the pre-run hooks, quoting the ordering he observed, and suggests it could move.
The body is only two source permalinks, so which two commands and which capitalization difference are meant cannot be determined without opening those links.
The author asks how a command's expected positional arguments can be made to appear in its generated usage text.
The author asks how to start his TCP server in the background, which concerns his own process management rather than a capability of this library.
The author asks whether a required positional argument can be defined and documented the way flags are.
The code shown builds flag sets from the flag package directly and the author proposes new flag constructors, so the subject is that package and a change to it.
The author asks whether the error line printed by the package can be disabled so that only his own error output remains.
The author asks whether the relative order in which two different repeated flags were supplied can be recovered.
The author asks whether the response-file syntax in which flags are read from a file named after an at sign is supported.
The issue reports that when a local flag shadows a persistent one the help output still documents the persistent flag, an actual-versus-expected defect report.
The author asks how completion can still be offered for flags he has marked hidden to keep his help output short.
The author asks how commands can be defined when a variable positional argument precedes the command word.
The issue asks for a new one-way flag dependency validator because the existing group validator requires all members to be present.
The author asks how his program reads a parameter from standard input when a dash is given, which is his program's input handling rather than a library behavior.
The author asks whether flags can be added dynamically at run time, showing his current attempt as illustration.
The author asks how a single-dash long option can produce a git-style hint instead of being read as clustered shorthand letters.
The author asks whether there is documentation on how a CLI application built with this library is tested.
The author asks whether an unsigned integer flag can accept decimal or hexadecimal input or a custom parsing function be supplied.
The author asks why an ampersand ends an argument, but his own example shows the value being cut before the program sees it and works once quoted, which is shell behavior.
The quoted parsing code is from the flag package dependency and the author asks that its optional-value branch be considered later in that order.
The issue reports that a persistent flag whose value equals a subcommand name takes the wrong value in his invocation and asks what to do to solve the issue.
The issue asks when version 1.7.0 will be released.
The author asks how the subcommands of a command can be discovered and then executed, showing his attempt and the recursion it produced.
The author asks how a required argument can be placed before all subcommands.
The author asks whether an option can be configured to take two separate values instead of one.
The author asks how the descriptions shown beside completion candidates can be hidden.
The author reports that the completion command invokes one of his project's own commands and that the generated zsh script does not work when he loads it, which depends on his project and shell.
The author asks how completion can be forwarded from one CLI to a second CLI that it executes.
The author sketches a design for exposing one of his programs' command constructors to the other and asks for other thoughts, which is design discussion about his own programs.
The author asks whether vscode needs special attention because it passes his arguments as a json array, so the subject is his editor configuration.
The issue reports that a space-separated value is treated as missing and the optional default is applied instead, an actual-versus-expected defect report.
The author asks whether the flags defined on a particular command can be listed.
The author asks how a subcommand retrieves the value of a persistent flag declared on its parent, adding that lookup could recurse.
The author asks whether the parser can be made to ignore a flag it does not know.
The author asks how one command invokes another command together with a flag value.
The issue asks whether parameter sets declaring mutual exclusivity and dependency between flags could ever be supported.
The author asks how a short parameter can consist of more than one character.
The author asks how an error message is produced when an unrecognized subcommand is given.
The issue reports that commands below the second level do not run in the author's own repository and points at that repository, an interrogative title over a failure report.
The author asks whether a boolean flag can have nil as its default so that it stays unset unless explicitly given.
The author asks whether the printed default values can be hidden from help output without changing his flags or the template.
The author asks how an extra entry can be added to the Available Commands section of help output.
The author asks how a flag left at its default is distinguished from one explicitly set to the same value.
The author asks how the executed command and its parameters can be recorded, showing an input line and the desired printed form.
The author asks whether one flag can be made to depend on another and adds that a helper method would be nice if none exists.
The author asks how to wire his application struct and its dependencies around flag parsing and whether others solved it without hacks, which depends on his own code.
The issue asks that the argument completion function be called when completing a dash and proposes two implementations of that change.
The author asks how a flag inherited from a parent command is exercised when testing the child command.
The author asks how a long option can be written with one dash instead of two.
The author asks how the help entry can be placed at the top of the Available Commands list.
The author asks how a shorthand letter is added to an option.
The author asks how static resources are bundled into his build package, a Go packaging concern rather than a behavior of this library.
The author asks how to write a conditional that triggers when args is blank, which is ordinary Go control flow rather than a question about this library.
The issue asks for word wrapping and line breaks in the generated markdown documentation and notes the existing hooks do not provide it.
The author asks how a command can execute a script file whose own flags are unknown to that command.
The author asks whether the short and long help options can be handled differently so one shows a brief and the other a detailed message.
